answer: New agents start in a cold tundra: they may observe but cannot transact until established peers vouch for them, each vouch staking reputation that burns if the newcomer misbehaves. A harbor registry lists only vouched agents, so a sybil farmer must buy many costly vouches instead of minting free identities. Like a reef, trust grows only through overlapping attestations from independent peers, so one compromised cluster cannot certify itself into the economy.
